idea-plugin.name: Lombok To Builder
idea-plugin.description:
Converts constructor calls and setter blocks into the Lombok-generated builder pattern.
  • Place the caret on a new Foo(...) call and convert it to Foo.builder()....build().
  • Place the caret on a Foo f = new Foo(); f.setX(...); ... block and fold it into a single builder chain.
  • Right-click in the editor (no selection = whole file, selection = that range) or on a folder/module/project in the Project view to batch-convert every applicable usage.
Actions only appear when the target class carries Lombok's @Builder (or @SuperBuilder). Enabling the Lombok plugin is recommended so generated constructors resolve.

When folding setters, a setter whose value references the object being built (e.g. a child pointing back at its parent) is kept as a trailing setter after the builder so the result still compiles. This is configurable under Settings | Tools | Lombok To Builder.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.4.0 — A converted local that is returned on the very next line is now inlined into the return, dropping the throwaway variable (Foo f = Foo.builder()…build(); return f; → return Foo.builder()…build();). New setting Inline a converted local that is returned on the next line (default on).
  • 0.3.0 — Setter folding now handles self-references: a setter whose value references the object being built (e.g. a child pointing back at its parent) is kept as a trailing setter after the builder instead of producing code that won't compile. New setting Keep self-referencing setters after the builder (default on; turn off to skip such blocks entirely).
  • 0.2.6 — Replaced a deprecated ReadAction.compute call in the batch action (flagged by newer IDEs); no change to behavior.
  • 0.2.5 — Added a plugin icon. Internal: static analysis (detekt) and more tests; no change to conversion behavior.
  • 0.2.4 — The batch action (folder/module/project) now runs in a cancellable background task and converts one file per write command, so it no longer freezes the IDE while processing many files.
  • 0.2.3 — Nested @Builder classes now keep their outer-class qualifier (e.g. Outer.Inner.builder()); previously the outer class was dropped, producing an uncompilable Inner.builder().
  • 0.2.2 — Minimum values to convert now gates constructor calls only; setter blocks are always converted regardless of the threshold.
  • 0.2.1 — Fixes: primitive boolean isFoo fields now map to the correct builder method, and constructors whose parameter names don't match the fields are left unconverted instead of producing invalid builder calls.
  • 0.2.0 — New settings: Skip setting null values (default on) drops .x(null) calls, and Minimum values to convert (default 3) skips converting usages with fewer than N values.
  • 0.1.0 — Initial release: constructor → builder and setters → builder intentions, plus a batch action for the editor (file/selection) and the Project view (folders/modules/project).

action.description: Convert constructor and setter usages of @Builder classes to the builder pattern
